issues.legal_issue: A suit seeking completion of a canal to carry water already allocated to a state is not a water dispute that ousts the Supreme Court’s jurisdiction when it does not seek a decision on the allocation or control of river waters.
material_facts: The suit sought an order requiring completion of the unfinished canal so the plaintiff state could use water already allocated to it.
The water-allocation dispute was before a tribunal, but the canal-construction issue was not among the matters referred to it.
The pleadings, read as a whole, concerned the obligation to complete the canal rather than the allocation or control of river water.
issues.conclusion: The suit was maintainable and was not barred by Article 262 of the Constitution read with Section 11 of the Inter-State Water Disputes Act, 1956.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 262 and Sections 2(c) and 11 of the Inter-State Water Disputes Act, 1956, jurisdiction is barred for a dispute referable to a tribunal that concerns the use, distribution or control of inter-State river waters, or the interpretation or implementation of an agreement concerning those matters. Whether a suit raises such a dispute is determined by considering the plaint and relief as a whole, not isolated averments, as held in State of Karnataka v. State of Andhra Pradesh, 2000 (9) SCC 572. Section 14 of the Act referred the water-sharing matters in paragraphs 9.1 and 9.2 of the Punjab Settlement to a tribunal, but not the canal-construction matter in paragraph 9.3; that distinction supported the conclusion that canal completion was not a water dispute under Section 2(c).

rule.if: inter_state_suit and relief_seeks_canal_completion and water_allocation_already_made and canal_issue_not_referred_for_water_adjudication

predicates.inter_state_suit: A state brought an original suit against another state, with or without the Union as a defendant.
predicates.relief_seeks_canal_completion: The plaintiff sought an order requiring completion of a canal to carry water.
predicates.water_allocation_already_made: The water the plaintiff sought to carry had already been allocated to it.
predicates.canal_issue_not_referred_for_water_adjud: The canal-construction issue was not among the water-sharing matters referred for adjudication.

issues.definition: When an inter-state suit seeks completion of a canal to carry already allocated water, and canal construction was not referred for water adjudication, the suit is not barred from the Supreme Court’s jurisdiction.

issues.legal_issue: A state’s suit is not defeated by limitation or laches where the opposing state does not seriously press that defence and the plaintiff alleges an ongoing failure to perform the obligation in dispute.
material_facts: The defendant state had pleaded that the suit was barred by limitation.
During the hearing, the defendant state did not seriously press the limitation issue, and its written submissions did not raise it.
The plaintiff alleged that the failure to complete the canal continued and that its cause of action was ongoing.
issues.conclusion: The suit could not be dismissed on limitation or laches; the Court answered the issue in favour of the plaintiff without undertaking an in-depth inquiry into limitation.
issues.legal_principle: The Court concluded that the suit could not be thrown out on limitation or laches, but expressly did not undertake an in-depth inquiry because the defendant state did not seriously press the issue. Article 112 of the Limitation Act and the rules concerning limitation for suits in the Supreme Court were discussed as submissions of counsel, not as a basis for a separate determination.

predicates.inter_state_suit: A state brought an original suit against another state, with or without the Union as a defendant.
predicates.defendant_did_not_seriously_press_limita: The defendant did not seriously pursue its pleaded limitation defence during the hearing.
predicates.ongoing_failure_alleged: The plaintiff alleged that the failure giving rise to the suit was continuing.

issues.definition: In an inter-state suit, when the defendant does not seriously pursue limitation and the plaintiff alleges a continuing failure, the suit is not thrown out on limitation or laches.

issues.legal_issue: A state that agreed to complete an unfinished canal needed to carry another state’s allocated water must fulfil that obligation, and the Union must secure completion if the state fails to do so.
material_facts: The plaintiff state had an allocated share of river water, and the existing canal system could carry only part of that share.

The canal was agreed upon as the means of enabling the plaintiff to use its allocation; the 1981 agreement required its completion, and the 1985 settlement stated that its construction would continue and be completed.
The plaintiff had completed the canal within its territory, while most of the portion in the defendant state’s territory had been constructed, leaving unfinished sections.
Substantial public funds had been spent on the project, and completion would allow the plaintiff to use its existing allocation without authorizing it to draw more water than allocated.
The Union had provided financial assistance and had a role in ensuring compliance with the inter-state agreements, but the canal remained incomplete.
issues.conclusion: The Court granted a mandatory injunction directing the defendant state to complete the unfinished canal and make it functional; if it failed to do so, the Union was directed to secure completion through its own agencies. The canal could carry only the water already allocated to the plaintiff, subject to any later directions following the tribunal’s decision.
issues.legal_principle: Section 78 of the Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966, provided for the determination of successor states’ rights and liabilities concerning the relevant water projects. The Court relied on the 1981 inter-state agreement and paragraph 9.3 of the 1985 Punjab Settlement as evidence of the canal-completion obligation; it held that a succeeding government remained duty bound to continue an unfinished governmental undertaking based on an inter-state consensus. Applying the requirements of a prima facie case, balance of convenience, and irreparable loss or injury, the Court found grounds for mandatory injunction. It also held that the Union had a duty to ensure implementation of the direction if the defendant state did not complete the work.

rule.if: inter_state_suit and inter_state_completion_commitment and claimant_has_allocated_water_share and existing_delivery_system_is_insufficient and canal_is_partly_completed

predicates.inter_state_suit: A state brought an original suit against another state, with or without the Union as a defendant.
predicates.inter_state_completion_commitment: The states had agreed that the defendant state would complete infrastructure needed to deliver the claimant’s allocation.
predicates.claimant_has_allocated_water_share: The claimant had an established allocation of the resource the infrastructure was intended to carry.
predicates.existing_delivery_system_is_insufficient: The existing delivery system could not carry the claimant’s full allocation.
predicates.canal_is_partly_completed: The claimant’s portion was complete and substantial work on the defendant’s portion had been done, but some work remained unfinished.

issues.definition: When states have committed to completing partly built infrastructure needed to deliver an established allocation that the existing system cannot carry, the defendant state must complete it and the Union must secure completion if that state fails.
